userStories.title: CI failure reader: GitLab and error handling
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend US-001's reader with head-bound GitLab failure logs and the shared listing/log error behavior for both forges.

**Motivation** — Sampled failures were real test failures in suites the local gates do not run (smoke, Postgres e2e, Python tests) and one dependency audit the branch did not cause.

**Approach** —
- **GitLab** (project segment `encodeProjectPath(ref.repo)`):
  1. Call `["glab", "api", "--hostname", ref.host, "projects/<enc>/merge_requests/<number>/pipelines?per_page=20"]`. The first entry whose `sha` equals `headSha` is the pipeline. When there is none, the result is `[]`.
  2. Call `["glab", "api", "--hostname", ref.host, "projects/<enc>/pipelines/<id>/jobs?scope[]=failed&per_page=100"]`. Jobs with `allow_failure: true` are dropped, and the first `MAX_FAILED_CHECKS` are kept.
  3. Read each job's log with `["glab", "api", "--hostname", ref.host, "projects/<enc>/jobs/<id>/trace"]`. `url` is the job's `web_url`, and `name` is its `name`.
- **Errors:**
  - A per-check log call that exits non-zero gives the excerpt `(log unavailable: <first stderr line>)`. It is not an error.
  - A listing call (check-runs, pipelines or jobs) that exits non-zero, or whose reply does not parse, throws `NaxError` code `FORGE_CI_READ_FAILED`.

Failure handling: CI listing call fails (non-zero or unparseable): `readFailedChecks` throws `FORGE_CI_READ_FAILED`; ledger `CI logs unavailable: <message>`, no repair, the PR stays a draft. One check's log call fails: that check's excerpt is `(log unavailable: <first stderr line>)`; the other checks are still read. No failed check found (or GitLab: no pipeline for the head): empty list; ledger `CI failed but no failed check was found for <head>`; no repair. The workflow ledger/decision half of these cases belongs to US-006.

**Scope** — In: extend existing src/forge/ci-failures.ts from US-001 and create test/unit/forge/ci-failures-gitlab.test.ts as the GitLab/error concern split. Reuse US-001's constants, ciExcerpt and barrel exports. Assert each listing boundary for both forges, including the GitLab jobs listing, and exact host/project argv using fake ForgeDeps. Out: US-001's URL and excerpt algorithms are not redesigned; workflow errors are consumed in US-006 and production wiring is US-008. The GitLab "CI status unavailable" case (no open MR found right after creation) was fixed in #2600 and is not addressed here. Re-running failed CI jobs (flake retry) and detecting failures the branch did not cause are not handled; such a failure costs one repair round and the PR stays a draft.

**Interface** — Preserve the public US-001 signature verbatim:
```ts
export async function readFailedChecks(
  ref: PrRef,
  headSha: string,
  deps: ForgeDeps,
  cwd: string,
): Promise<readonly FailedCheck[]>;
```
Use the existing NaxError stage/context/cause pattern, but use FORGE_CI_READ_FAILED rather than neighboring readers' FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE. No test touches a real forge or model, and no existing US-001-created file is declared as newly created here.

userStories.title: One CI readiness rule
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make pending CI hold workflow drafts, share strict-green readiness with promote, and allow a pending-only draft to retry publishing at the same HEAD.

**Motivation** — The CI rule differs by path.

**Approach** —
- **One CI rule.** `ciAllowsReady(outcome)` in `src/workflow/ci-wait.ts` is `outcome === "green"`. `ciReason` gives a reason for every `FeatureCiState` except `green` and `skipped`, which adds `pending`. Bot fix and promote call `ciAllowsReady`. `src/bot/` and `src/cli/` import it by relative path from the `ci-wait.ts` leaf, never through the `@/workflow` barrel: `src/cli/workflow-promote.ts:19-22` explains the cycle that barrel would close.
- **A pending draft is retryable.** Because `pending` now keeps a PR a draft, a re-run at the same HEAD publishes again (and waits for CI again) instead of stopping as already-finished, the way an `unavailable` draft does today. This applies only when the pending CI is the draft's sole reason (`reasons` has exactly one entry), so a draft held for an unrelated reason is not re-published on every run. A repair round already spent stays spent (`ciRepairRounds` carries over), which is accepted.

`ciReason` (`src/workflow/approval.ts`).
- Target: `pending` returns `detail ?? "CI still pending after the wait"`. `green` and `skipped` return `undefined`. The other states are unchanged.
- The comments that say pending never blocks are updated: `approval.ts:101-103` (W-R9), `ci-wait.ts:5`, `finalize.ts:61-64` (`ciDetailFields`) and `finalize.ts:530`. Comment edits do not grow `finalize.ts`.
- `DETAILED_CI_STATES` is unchanged, so a pending record keeps no `ciDetail` and its open item uses the fallback text, while the publish-time reason carries the wait's own detail. This is intended.

`isTransientDraft` (`src/workflow/feature.ts`).
- Target: a `draft` with `ci === "pending"` and exactly one entry in `reasons` is transient, like `ci === "unavailable"`.

`ciGreen` (`src/cli/workflow-promote.ts`).
- Target: `ciAllowsReady(result.outcome)`, with unchanged behaviour.

The user ruled 2026-10-21: strict green everywhere. This supersedes the earlier workflow ruling W-R9 ("CI pending does not block").

**Scope** — In: update ci-wait.ts, approval.ts, workflow-promote.ts, feature.ts and stale finalize.ts comments. open-items.ts already consumes ciReason and should gain pending behavior through that seam, not duplicate readiness logic. Preserve existing unavailable and PR-update-failure retries. Out: bot calls the helper in US-005; no marker or CI repair work here. The actual publish implementation does not gain a repair loop; US-006 changes publishStep instead.

**Interface** — `CiWaitOutcome = "green" | "failed" | "pending" | "conflicting" | "no-checks" | "unavailable"`; `ciAllowsReady(outcome)` is `outcome === "green"`; preserve `ciReason(ci: FeatureCiState | undefined, detail?: string): string | undefined`. Use the relative ci-wait leaf import in promote.

Regression migrations are part of implementation: in approval.test.ts change READY from pending to green, remove the W-R9 title clause, and remove pending from the green/pending/skipped nonblocking case. In open-items-kinds.test.ts remove pending from the no-ci-item case. In finalize.test.ts wire the promoted happy path as green and rename it CI green; also explicitly wire green in the deterministic-story-reason case to preserve its exact one reason and no-advisor invariant. In feature.test.ts preserve existing transient rows, add ["pending", "pending", ["no CI result within 1200000ms"]], and add a two-reason pending already-finished case. In finalize-ci-gate.test.ts replace the slow-CI W-R9 expectation with a kept draft, asked=[], and reasons containing the wait detail. In integration/workflow/feature-e2e.test.ts script a passing check `[{"name":"t","state":"SUCCESS","bucket":"pass"}]`, rename to CI green and pin ready/green, preserving the full review-fix-publish ready path. Add focused cases in ci-wait.test.ts, approval.test.ts, open-items-kinds.test.ts, workflow-promote.test.ts and feature.test.ts. Tests mock the wait/feature machine; never a live forge.

Under strict green a pending wait is a readiness reason, so the test becomes "slow CI (pending) keeps the draft and never asks the advisor", asserting that `asked` is `[]`, that the update kept the draft, and that the reasons contain the wait's detail. This keeps the invariant that the CI wait's outcome decides whether the advisor is asked.

userStories.title: Workflow PR marker
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Identify workflow PR bodies with a hidden marker that survives every body construction and truncation path.

**Motivation** — Run on a nax-workflow draft, it would promote a PR the workflow held.

**Approach** —
- **nax-workflow PRs are recognised by a hidden marker.** The workflow PR body starts with the line `<!-- nax-workflow:v1 -->`. A forged or copied marker can only make `nax bot fix` more careful (it keeps the draft), never less.

`buildWorkflowPrBody(input)` (`src/workflow/pr-body.ts`).
- Target: the body starts with `NAX_WORKFLOW_PR_MARKER` followed by a blank line, on every path including the truncated one.

Adds `NAX_WORKFLOW_PR_MARKER` and `hasNaxWorkflowMarker` to `src/forge/marker.ts`, exported from `@/forge`, and makes `buildWorkflowPrBody` start every body with the marker. `hasNaxWorkflowMarker(env.info.body)` is true when the body contains the marker line.

**Scope** — In: extend existing forge/marker.ts and forge/index.ts; prefix workflow/pr-body.ts without changing existing section order, Closes placement or the total PR_BODY_MAX_CHARS cap. Add ACs to existing test/unit/forge/marker.test.ts and test/unit/workflow/pr-body.test.ts. The body-order and Closes tests locate sections with indexOf and are unaffected; no existing assertion changes. Out: readiness holds consuming the marker are US-005; strict-green policy is US-003; do not alter nax-bot comment ownership or trust logic. Workflow PRs opened before this change carry no marker, so `nax bot fix` treats them as ordinary drafts and marks one ready once CI is green. No backfill or heuristic recognition.

**Interface** — `NAX_WORKFLOW_PR_MARKER` is `<!-- nax-workflow:v1 -->`; `hasNaxWorkflowMarker` consumes the PR body; `buildWorkflowPrBody(input)` preserves its existing input contract. Import marker symbols through @/forge in tests to verify public exports. Use deterministic oversized body inputs to exercise truncation, not live forge calls.

userStories.title: Bot fix waits for CI and preserves workflow drafts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make bot fix mark ordinary drafts ready only after green CI on the correct head, while keeping all marked workflow drafts for workflow promote.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix`'s `readyStep` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`) marks any draft PR ready, also on the `nothing` exit, and reads no CI state.

**Approach** — Bot fix ready step:

`readyStep` runs these checks in order:

1. **The PR is not a draft:** it returns `{ markedReady: false }` with exit `report` (unchanged).
2. **`hasNaxWorkflowMarker(env.info.body)` is true** (the body contains the marker line): it makes no forge call and returns `{ markedReady: false, readyHeld: "nax workflow PR: promote it with nax workflow promote" }`.
3. **Otherwise it waits for CI:**
   `_fixReportDeps.waitForChecks(env.ref.forge, env.info.url, { cwd: env.repoRoot, timeoutMs, pollMs, expectedSha: state.pushedSha ?? env.info.headSha })`.
   `timeoutMs` and `pollMs` come from `resolveWorkflowConfig(env.config).timeouts.ciWaitMs` and `.ciPollMs`.
   - If `ciAllowsReady(outcome)` is false, it returns `{ markedReady: false, readyHeld: "CI <outcome>: <detail>" }`.
   - If it is true, `markReadyArgv` runs as today (a non-zero exit still throws `BOT_FIX_READY_FAILED`), and it returns `{ markedReady: true }`.

`renderFixSummary` appends `Kept as draft: <readyHeld>` when `readyHeld` is set, and `Marked ready.` when `markedReady` is true. The `ready` node of `BOT_FIX_GRAPH` adds `"readyHeld"` to `produces`.

Adds the state field `readyHeld?: string`. Adds `waitForChecks` to `_fixReportDeps` (imported by relative path from `../workflow/ci-wait`), adds `readyHeld` to `BotFixState` and to the `ready` node's `produces`, and adds the two summary lines to `renderFixSummary`. Bot fix and promote call `ciAllowsReady`. `src/bot/` and `src/cli/` import it by relative path from the `ci-wait.ts` leaf, never through the `@/workflow` barrel: `src/cli/workflow-promote.ts:19-22` explains the cycle that barrel would close.

**Scope** — In: fix-report.ts readiness and summary, fix-steps.ts state, fix-run.ts graph output declaration, existing integration/bot/fix-report.test.ts and fix-graph.test.ts. Every readyStep return remains a StepResult with patch and exit report. Existing draft readyStep tests must stub `_fixReportDeps.waitForChecks` to `{ outcome: "green", detail: "all checks passed" }` before their unchanged mark-ready success/failure assertions; preserve the ready PR no-op and BOT_FIX_READY_FAILED invariants. Exercise the actual readyStep through runStepGraph(BOT_FIX_GRAPH, ...) for both nothing-route seams, rather than stubbing readiness itself. Out: US-003 and US-004 own shared policy and marker production. `nax bot fix` does not repair CI on any PR; CI repair runs only inside `nax run`, after publish, on the PR the workflow published. PR-thread rulings (a reply on a nax bot thread counts as the ruling), and posting the workflow's flagged rulings and advisor holds as PR threads, are B4 part 3, a later spec; until then `nax bot fix` never marks a nax-workflow draft ready. The `nax bot fix` CI wait has no early exit for a repository without CI; such a repository waits `workflow.timeouts.ciWaitMs` and keeps the draft.

**Interface** — `readyStep(env, state)`, `readyHeld?: string`, and the exact wait call above compose the upstream `hasNaxWorkflowMarker` and `ciAllowsReady` contracts. Reuse `markReadyArgv(forge, prRef)` and existing NaxError behavior. Tests import bot/config/forge symbols through public barrels, fake waits and commands, and restore _deps; no real CI wait, forge or model.

userStories.title: CI repair decision after publish
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the persisted/configurable CI repair contract and make publishStep route failed PR CI to a repair decision without changing the publish implementation.

**Motivation** — The largest draft reason was "CI failed" (18).

**Approach** —
- **`publish` itself does not change.** `finalize.ts` is at 599 of 600 allowed lines. The repair decision is made in `publishStep` (`src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`) after `env.steps.publish` returns, through a new optional step `env.steps.readCiFailures`. The G0 equivalence harness supplies no such step, so every golden trace stays byte-identical.
- **The repair session is `env.steps.branchFix`.** `ciRepairStep` passes the failing checks as findings (`kind: "gate"`, severity `important`, ids `C1..Cn`), exactly as `gateRepairStep` passes red-gate excerpts (ids `G1..`). `ciRepairDecision` and `ciRepairStep` live in `feature-steps.ts`, next to `gateRepairStep`, because they use its module-private `limitsOf`, `costExceeded` and `roundLabel`. The file is 468 lines. US-007 implements ciRepairStep; this story implements ciRepairDecision.

- **Config:** `workflow.ciRepairRounds`, an integer `>= 0`, default `1`. `buildFeatureEnv` (`src/workflow/feature-env.ts`) wires it into `FeatureLimits`, as it does `finalGateRepairRounds`. `DEFAULT_LIMITS` (`feature-steps.ts`) reads `WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS.ciRepairRounds`. US-008 owns buildFeatureEnv wiring.
- **Decision.** `ciRepairDecision(env, rec, out, head)` in `feature-steps.ts` is called by `publishStep` after `env.steps.publish` returns. It is a separate function, to stay under the complexity gate. It returns findings (route to `ci-repair`) or nothing.
  - **When it runs:** it calls `env.steps.readCiFailures({ url: out.url, head })` only when all of these hold:
    - `out.outcome === "draft"` and `out.ci === "failed"`;
    - `out.url` is set, and the head was read;
    - `env.steps.readCiFailures` exists;
    - `(rec.ciRepairRounds ?? 0) < (limitsOf(env).ciRepairRounds ?? 0)`;
    - `costExceeded(env)` is false.
  - **On a non-empty list:** it writes the ledger note `CI failed: <names joined ", "> (repairing)`, and `publishStep` returns its usual patch plus `ciRepairFindings`, with exit `"ci-repair"`.
    - Each finding is `{ kind: "gate", severity: "important", issue: "CI check <name> failed:\n<excerpt>" }`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Consume failed-check findings in a bounded graph-native branch-fix session, rerun local gates, and publish/wait again.

**Motivation** — Fixing them is manual today.

**Approach** —
- **Graph-native repair loop.** The repair loops through graph transitions (`publish` -> `ci-repair` -> `final-gates` -> `publish`), the same shape as `final-gates` -> `gate-repair` -> `final-gates`. There is no inline retry loop (`.nax/rules/retry-strategy.md`).
- **The repair session is `env.steps.branchFix`.** `ciRepairStep` passes the failing checks as findings (`kind: "gate"`, severity `important`, ids `C1..Cn`), exactly as `gateRepairStep` passes red-gate excerpts (ids `G1..`). `ciRepairDecision` and `ciRepairStep` live in `feature-steps.ts`, next to `gateRepairStep`, because they use its module-private `limitsOf`, `costExceeded` and `roundLabel`. The file is 468 lines.

- **`ciRepairStep(env, rec)`** in `feature-steps.ts` mirrors `gateRepairStep`.
  - `round = (rec.ciRepairRounds ?? 0) + 1`.
  - If `round > limit`, it writes the ledger note `CI repair skipped: round <round> is past workflow.ciRepairRounds (<limit>)` and returns `{ patch: {} }`.
  - If `rec.ciRepairFindings` is empty or absent (a resume), it returns `{ patch: { ciRepairRounds: round } }` and makes no `branchFix` call.
  - Otherwise:
    - The findings get ids `C1..Cn`.
    - It writes the ledger note `CI repair r<round>: <n> item(s): C1, ...`.
    - It logs the step start line `roundLabel("ci-repair", round)` on `env.steps.modelFor?.("branch-fix")`.
    - It calls `env.steps.branchFix(findings)`.
    - It writes the same three conditional notes as gate repair: `CI repair session failed: <failure>`, `auto-committed the CI repair's edits`, and `CI repair left uncommitted edits: the auto-commit failed`.
    - Mirroring follows gate repair: the `CI failed ... (repairing)`, `CI failed but no failed check ...`, `CI logs unavailable ...`, `CI repair r<n> ...`, `CI repair skipped ...` and `CI repair session failed ...` notes are written with `NO_MIRROR`; the two auto-commit notes are mirrored.
    - It returns `{ patch: { ciRepairRounds: round, ciRepairFindings: undefined } }`.
- **After the repair:** `final-gates` re-runs the repo gates (see the reuse rule above), and its existing repair and red handling applies. Then `publish` runs again: it pushes the repair commit, finds the open draft, waits for CI on the new head, and keeps or promotes the PR by the usual rules.
- **Cost stop:** `hasAgentWork("ci-repair", rec)` is true when `rec.ciRepairFindings` is non-empty, so the existing `costStop` (skip to `final-gates`, `costLimited: true`) covers the node. `ciRepairDecision` checks `costExceeded` itself, so a cost-limited run does not loop.

`FEATURE_GRAPH` (`src/workflow/feature-graph.ts`).
- Target: `publish` declares `exits: ["ci-repair"]` with transitions `[{ on: "ci-repair", to: "ci-repair" }, { to: "done" }]`, and adds `"ciRepairFindings"` to its `produces`.
- A new node `ci-repair`: `kind: "agent"`, `commits: true`, `produces: ["ciRepairRounds", "ciRepairFindings"]`, transitions `[{ to: "final-gates" }]`, `run: ciRepairStep`.

`finalGatesStep` (`src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`).
- Target: it reuses them only when `!rec.fixRan && !rec.ciRepairRounds`.

Failure handling: Repair session fails or changes nothing: ledger note; `final-gates` and `publish` run again; CI stays failed; no further round once the limit is reached. Rounds used up, or cost limit reached: no repair; publish outcome as today. An absent optional CI round limit reads as zero.

**Scope** — In: ciRepairStep, final-gate reuse, hasAgentWork/cost handling, FEATURE_GRAPH declarations and transitions, new feature-steps-ci-repair.test.ts, existing feature-graph.test.ts tables, and actual runFeatureMachine seam tests using US-006's ciFailures/publishedSeq harness. Update the exact node list, transitions, exits, produces, kinds and committing-node list; ci-repair is an agent and a committing node. Do not change the existing branchFix session's G/B numbering, permission resolution or auto-commit implementation. Keep feature-steps.ts within its size limit and split small helpers if needed without moving private-limit consumers away from the specified file. Out: US-006 owns decision/config/record shapes; US-008 owns production readers/reporting; no inline retry, new model operation, or repair re-review. Re-running failed CI jobs (flake retry) and detecting failures the branch did not cause are not handled; such a failure costs one repair round and the PR stays a draft.

**Interface** — `env.steps.branchFix(findings: readonly WorkflowFinding[]): Promise<BranchFixOutcome>`, with `BranchFixOutcome { reply?, failure?, autoCommitted: boolean, dirty: boolean }` (`src/workflow/branch-fix.ts`). The new node consumes US-006's ciRepairFindings and patches ciRepairRounds plus cleared findings. Tests exercise this producer/consumer seam through runFeatureMachine, with fake agent/forge steps, as well as direct cap, empty-findings, note-order and log-label assertions.

**Goal** — Connect the graph to the production forge CI reader and make repair rounds visible in approval evidence and run reporting.

**Motivation** — Fixing them is manual today.

**Approach** —

A URL with no number throws `NaxError` code `WORKFLOW_CI_PR_URL`.

The schema/default-limit changes are supplied by US-006; this story owns the real environment wiring.
- **Reporting:**
  - `repairEvidence(record)` returns the gate-repair line verbatim. When `ciRepairRounds` is set, it then returns `CI repair: <n> round(s) after CI failed on the PR; the repair diff was not re-reviewed`.
  - `buildWorkflowRunSummary` records `ciRepairRounds` when it is non-zero, as it does `gateRepairRounds`.
  - `reportWorkflowRun`'s summary line prints `CI repair rounds <n>`.

`approvalEvidence` (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`).
- Target: its gate-repair lines move to a new `repairEvidence(record)` in `src/workflow/repair-evidence.ts`, which also returns the CI-repair line. `finalize.ts` must not grow.

- Target: adds `ciRepairRounds?: number`, beside `gateRepairRounds`.

Failure handling: PR URL has no number: `readCiFailuresFor` throws `WORKFLOW_CI_PR_URL`; handled as a read failure. CI listing call fails (non-zero or unparseable): `readFailedChecks` throws `FORGE_CI_READ_FAILED`; ledger `CI logs unavailable: <message>`, no repair, the PR stays a draft. This story supplies the real throwing reader; US-006 supplies its fail-soft decision consumer.
